=LIVE EVENT - ~3 hours from the time this is posted= SpaceX will be launching a commercially loaded rocket and attempting to land it on a barge in the ocean

Should be interesting. They very recently succesfully landed a rocket back on Earth. This was a major game changer for humanity in space and for the space industry. Currently we simply dispose of rockets after they launch and just 5 years ago most would have said what SpaceX did by safely landing it back on Earth would have been impossible. Imagine a rocket taller than most buildings going thousands of miles an hour... in space - now try to bring it back through the atmosphere and land it on a square zone smaller than the size of a football field - oh and if it tips over, lands too hard, or if's just in a bad mood it'll probably explode. They did that.

Today they're going to try to one up that and land it on a barge, the so-called drone ship, in the middle of the ocean. Success here would mean they can basically land their rockets anywhere which has huge implications for reuse. Today we launch a rocket, destroy it, spend tens of millions of dollars and months of time building another from scratch, and then finally launch it again. Imagine a future where we're launching rockets, returning and refitting them back at mobile rocket ports in the sea, and relaunching in a matter of hours. Today's test will probably not succeed, but it's going to be an exciting sweat and even if it does fail we'll get to see some nice fire works or at least a big splash.
